benchmarks.label: Brent

peak.note: Futures intraday wartime high (Wikipedia chronology). Physical Dated Brent (EIA spot via FRED) peaked at $138.21 on 2026-04-07 and was $114.89 on 2026-09-22.

benchmarks.note: Fell to about $91.99/bbl by 09:20 GMT on 18 Nov (Reuters), down 1.2% on the day and on track for a ~20% monthly decline, as US crude stocks rose 5.28 million barrels (EIA, week to 13 Nov) and Middle East exports kept recovering. Losses were limited by a fresh round of US-Iran strikes: the US hit an IRGC missile site on Qeshm Island on 17 Nov after an Iranian drone attack on the US base in Bahrain, and Houthi drones targeted East-West pipeline pumping stations.

note: Oil extended its slide on 18 November: Brent fell to about $91.99/bbl (-1.2%) and WTI to $84.34 (-2%) by 09:20 GMT (Reuters), as US crude and gasoline stockpiles rose in the week to 13 Nov and recovering Middle East exports pointed to a Q4 supply surplus; both benchmarks were on track for a roughly 20% monthly decline. The losses were capped by a fresh round of US-Iran strikes — Iran's IRGC claimed a drone attack on the US base in Bahrain on 17 Nov, which CENTCOM said it intercepted, and the US then struck an IRGC missile site on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz the same day — plus Houthi drones aimed at Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline pumping stations. TTF fell 3.2% to about €82.66/MWh and JKM was little changed near $27.77; Henry Hub held near $3.21, still largely insulated from the Gulf and Red Sea turmoil.
